name_note: GTDB R232 places Gardnerella within Bifidobacterium as B. vaginale and splits it into several species; the genomes in s__Bifidobacterium vaginale_H are labelled Gardnerella vaginalis or Gardnerella sp. in NCBI, and no published name is specific to this lineage.

sentences.text: The organism is one of the genomic species of the group known in the literature as Gardnerella, whose members are associated with bacterial vaginosis but are also isolated from healthy individuals.
Molecular approaches expanded the genus Gardnerella to several species that differ in virulence potential, and it now covers six validly named species together with further genomospecies.
Two of those species, Gardnerella pickettii and Gardnerella greenwoodii, were proposed from urine of a patient diagnosed with overactive bladder and of a healthy postmenopausal woman.
In vaginal swabs from 101 individuals with bacterial vaginosis and 150 without, concentrations and prevalence of each Gardnerella species group were significantly higher in those with the condition.
A study of pregnant women reported that individual vaginal microbiomes often contained multiple Gardnerella variants, and that the number of clades was associated with increased microbial load.
